## C5. Subject-coupled NB contrasts and 16-gene aggregate

```{r}
#| label: panel-c-effects

panel_c_n_boot <- 2000L
panel_c_effects_cache_id <- paste(
  "v5_subject_coupled_nb_bayesian_bootstrap_independent_hca_gene_draws",
  paste0("n_boot=", panel_c_n_boot),
  paste0("sample=", panel_c_sample_cache_id),
  paste0("hca=", panel_c_hca_grid_id),
  "dispersion=edgeR_trended_all_shared_genes",
  "repeat_libraries=sum_counts_and_exposure",
  sep = "|"
)

rebuild_panel_c_effects <- isTRUE(params$run_panel_c_rebuild) ||
  isTRUE(rebuild_panel_c_sample) ||
  isTRUE(rebuild_panel_c_hca) ||
  !file.exists(panel_c_effects_rds)

if (!rebuild_panel_c_effects) {
  panel_c_effects_cache <- readRDS(panel_c_effects_rds)
  if (is.list(panel_c_effects_cache) &&
      identical(panel_c_effects_cache$cache_id, panel_c_effects_cache_id) &&
      is.data.frame(panel_c_effects_cache$data)) {
    panel_c_effects <- panel_c_effects_cache$data
    message("Loaded panel-c effects: ", nrow(panel_c_effects), " rows")
  } else {
    message("Ignoring stale Panel-c effects cache: inputs or policy changed.")
    rebuild_panel_c_effects <- TRUE
  }
}

if (rebuild_panel_c_effects) {
  panel_c_signature_ids <- panel_c_feature_map$.feature[
    match(panel_c_gene_order, panel_c_feature_map$gene)
  ]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(panel_c_signature_ids), !anyDuplicated(panel_c_signature_ids))

  log_sum_exp <- function(x) {
    m <- max(x)
    m + log(sum(exp(x - m)))
  }

  # One independent column per subject×state. For repeated libraries, add raw
  # counts and add their model exposures exp(offset) before returning to log scale.
  collapse_subject_state <- function(counts, meta) {
    keys <- meta |>
      dplyr::distinct(.data$subject_id, .data$group) |>
      dplyr::arrange(.data$group, .data$subject_id) |>
      dplyr::mutate(sample_key = paste(.data$subject_id, .data$group, sep = "__"))

    collapsed_counts <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
      idx <- which(
        meta$subject_id == keys$subject_id[[i]] &
          meta$group == keys$group[[i]]
      )
      rowSums(counts[, meta$col_id[idx], drop = FALSE])
    }))
    colnames(collapsed_counts) <- keys$sample_key
    rownames(collapsed_counts) <- rownames(counts)

    keys$offset <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
      idx <- which(
        meta$subject_id == keys$subject_id[[i]] &
          meta$group == keys$group[[i]]
      )
      log_sum_exp(meta$offset[idx])
    }, numeric(1))

    list(counts = collapsed_counts, meta = keys)
  }

  panel_c_subject_data <- collapse_subject_state(
    panel_c_counts,
    panel_c_sample_meta
  )

  # Estimate NB dispersions with all shared genes, not just the selected 16.
  fit_panel_c_dispersion <- function(counts, meta, design) {
    dge <- edgeR::DGEList(counts = counts, samples = meta)
    dge$offset <- matrix(
      meta$offset,
      nrow = nrow(dge),
      ncol = ncol(dge),
      byrow = TRUE
    )
    keep <- edgeR::filterByExpr(dge, design = design)
    signature_idx <- match(panel_c_signature_ids, rownames(dge))
    stopifnot(!anyNA(signature_idx))
    keep[signature_idx] <- TRUE
    dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
    dge <- edgeR::estimateDisp(dge, design, robust = TRUE)
    fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(dge, design, robust = TRUE)
    dispersion <- if (!is.null(dge$trended.dispersion)) {
      dge$trended.dispersion
    } else if (!is.null(dge$tagwise.dispersion)) {
      dge$tagwise.dispersion
    } else {
      rep_len(dge$common.dispersion, nrow(dge))
    }
    names(dispersion) <- rownames(dge)
    list(dge = dge, fit = fit, dispersion = dispersion)
  }

  subject_counts <- panel_c_subject_data$counts
  subject_meta <- panel_c_subject_data$meta

  uc_meta <- subject_meta |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$group %in% c("control", "untreated")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(group = factor(.data$group, levels = c("control", "untreated")))
  uc_counts <- subject_counts[, uc_meta$sample_key, drop = FALSE]
  uc_design <- stats::model.matrix(~ 0 + group, data = uc_meta)
  colnames(uc_design) <- sub("^group", "", colnames(uc_design))
  uc_fit <- fit_panel_c_dispersion(uc_counts, uc_meta, uc_design)
  uc_dispersion <- unname(uc_fit$dispersion[panel_c_signature_ids])

  paired_subjects <- intersect(
    subject_meta$subject_id[subject_meta$group == "untreated"],
    subject_meta$subject_id[subject_meta$group == "treated"]
  )
  paired_meta <- subject_meta |>
    dplyr::filter(
      .data$subject_id %in% paired_subjects,
      .data$group %in% c("untreated", "treated")
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      subject_id = factor(.data$subject_id, levels = sort(paired_subjects)),
      state = factor(.data$group, levels = c("treated", "untreated"))
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$subject_id, .data$state)
  paired_counts <- subject_counts[, paired_meta$sample_key, drop = FALSE]
  paired_design <- stats::model.matrix(~ subject_id + state, data = paired_meta)
  paired_fit <- fit_panel_c_dispersion(paired_counts, paired_meta, paired_design)
  paired_dispersion <- unname(paired_fit$dispersion[panel_c_signature_ids])

  signature_counts_uc <- uc_counts[panel_c_signature_ids, , drop = FALSE]
  signature_counts_paired <- paired_counts[panel_c_signature_ids, , drop = FALSE]

  mglm_signature <- function(counts, offsets, dispersion, weights = NULL) {
    as.numeric(edgeR::mglmOneGroup(
      counts,
      offset = offsets,
      dispersion = dispersion,
      weights = weights
    ))
  }

  draw_dirichlet_weights <- function(n) {
    w <- stats::rexp(n)
    n * w / sum(w)
  }

  # A common subject-weight vector is used for every gene in a replicate. This
  # is the key coupling that the previous gene-bootstrap aggregate did not
  # preserve. Continuous positive weights also avoid infinite MLEs caused by a
  # discrete bootstrap replicate containing only zero-count subjects.
  bayes_bootstrap_unpaired <- function(n_boot, seed) {
    idx_u <- which(uc_meta$group == "untreated")
    idx_c <- which(uc_meta$group == "control")
    out_u <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = length(panel_c_gene_order))
    out_c <- out_u
    set.seed(seed)
    for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
      wu <- draw_dirichlet_weights(length(idx_u))
      wc <- draw_dirichlet_weights(length(idx_c))
      out_u[b, ] <- mglm_signature(
        signature_counts_uc[, idx_u, drop = FALSE],
        uc_meta$offset[idx_u],
        uc_dispersion,
        weights = wu
      )
      out_c[b, ] <- mglm_signature(
        signature_counts_uc[, idx_c, drop = FALSE],
        uc_meta$offset[idx_c],
        uc_dispersion,
        weights = wc
      )
    }
    colnames(out_u) <- panel_c_gene_order
    colnames(out_c) <- panel_c_gene_order
    list(untreated = out_u, control = out_c)
  }

  bayes_bootstrap_paired <- function(n_boot, seed) {
    key <- paste(as.character(paired_meta$subject_id), paired_meta$group, sep = "__")
    out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = length(panel_c_gene_order))
    set.seed(seed)
    for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
      w <- draw_dirichlet_weights(length(paired_subjects))
      iu <- match(paste(paired_subjects, "untreated", sep = "__"), key)
      it <- match(paste(paired_subjects, "treated", sep = "__"), key)
      u <- mglm_signature(
        signature_counts_paired[, iu, drop = FALSE],
        paired_meta$offset[iu],
        paired_dispersion,
        weights = w
      )
      t <- mglm_signature(
        signature_counts_paired[, it, drop = FALSE],
        paired_meta$offset[it],
        paired_dispersion,
        weights = w
      )
      out[b, ] <- u - t
    }
    colnames(out) <- panel_c_gene_order
    out
  }

  uc_boot <- bayes_bootstrap_unpaired(panel_c_n_boot, seed = 20260809L)
  paired_boot <- bayes_bootstrap_paired(panel_c_n_boot, seed = 20260810L)

  hca_matrix <- panel_c_hca_draws |>
    dplyr::select(.data$.draw, .data$gene, .data$hca_log_mu) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = .data$gene, values_from = .data$hca_log_mu) |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$.draw)
  stopifnot(all(panel_c_gene_order %in% names(hca_matrix)))
  hca_draw_id <- hca_matrix$.draw
  hca_matrix <- as.matrix(hca_matrix[, panel_c_gene_order, drop = FALSE])

  # Each gene was fitted in a separate brms model. Equal numeric draw indices
  # therefore are not joint posterior draws and must not be used to manufacture
  # cross-gene dependence. Sample one posterior draw independently per gene,
  # while retaining the genuine across-gene coupling in each SAVI Bayesian-
  # bootstrap draw.
  set.seed(20260811L)
  hca_idx <- matrix(
    sample.int(
      nrow(hca_matrix),
      panel_c_n_boot * length(panel_c_gene_order),
      replace = TRUE
    ),
    nrow = panel_c_n_boot,
    ncol = length(panel_c_gene_order),
    dimnames = list(NULL, panel_c_gene_order)
  )
  hca_pair <- vapply(seq_along(panel_c_gene_order), function(j) {
    hca_matrix[hca_idx[, j], j]
  }, numeric(panel_c_n_boot))
  colnames(hca_pair) <- panel_c_gene_order

  delta_matrices <- list(
    "untreated - study control" =
      (uc_boot$untreated - uc_boot$control) / log(2),
    "untreated - HCA" =
      (uc_boot$untreated - hca_pair) / log(2),
    "paired untreated - treated" = paired_boot / log(2),
    "study control - HCA" =
      (uc_boot$control - hca_pair) / log(2)
  )

  n_untreated <- sum(uc_meta$group == "untreated")
  n_control <- sum(uc_meta$group == "control")
  n_paired <- length(paired_subjects)
  n_hca_donors <- panel_b_hca_comprehensive_n_donors

  effects <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      delta_matrices[["untreated - study control"]],
      panel_c_gene_order,
      "untreated - study control",
      "subject-level Bayesian bootstrap of NB cohort locations",
      n_untreated,
      n_control
    ),
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      delta_matrices[["untreated - HCA"]],
      panel_c_gene_order,
      "untreated - HCA",
      "subject-level Bayesian bootstrap independently paired with HCA posterior",
      n_untreated,
      n_hca_donors
    ),
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      delta_matrices[["paired untreated - treated"]],
      panel_c_gene_order,
      "paired untreated - treated",
      "paired-subject Bayesian bootstrap of NB cohort locations",
      n_paired,
      n_paired
    ),
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      delta_matrices[["study control - HCA"]],
      panel_c_gene_order,
      "study control - HCA",
      "subject-level Bayesian bootstrap independently paired with HCA posterior",
      n_control,
      n_hca_donors
    )
  ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$contrast) |>
    dplyr::mutate(q_value = stats::p.adjust(.data$tail_p, method = "BH")) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  aggregate_matrices <- lapply(delta_matrices, function(x) {
    matrix(rowMeans(x), ncol = 1L)
  })
  agg <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      aggregate_matrices[["untreated - study control"]],
      "16-gene covered subset",
      "untreated - study control",
      "subject-coupled 16-gene Bayesian bootstrap",
      n_untreated,
      n_control,
      is_aggregate = TRUE
    ),
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      aggregate_matrices[["untreated - HCA"]],
      "16-gene covered subset",
      "untreated - HCA",
      "subject-coupled Bayesian bootstrap independently paired with HCA posterior",
      n_untreated,
      n_hca_donors,
      is_aggregate = TRUE
    ),
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      aggregate_matrices[["paired untreated - treated"]],
      "16-gene covered subset",
      "paired untreated - treated",
      "paired-subject-coupled 16-gene Bayesian bootstrap",
      n_paired,
      n_paired,
      is_aggregate = TRUE
    ),
    summarise_panel_c_draw_matrix(
      aggregate_matrices[["study control - HCA"]],
      "16-gene covered subset",
      "study control - HCA",
      "subject-coupled Bayesian bootstrap independently paired with HCA posterior",
      n_control,
      n_hca_donors,
      is_aggregate = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(q_value = stats::p.adjust(.data$tail_p, method = "BH"))

  panel_c_effects <- dplyr::bind_rows(agg, effects) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = factor(
        .data$gene,
        levels = c("16-gene covered subset", panel_c_gene_order)
      ),
      contrast = factor(.data$contrast, levels = panel_c_contrast_levels)
    )

  panel_c_effects_cache <- list(
    data = panel_c_effects,
    cache_id = panel_c_effects_cache_id,
    paired_subjects = paired_subjects,
    hca_draw_ids_sampled = matrix(
      hca_draw_id[hca_idx],
      nrow = panel_c_n_boot,
      ncol = length(panel_c_gene_order),
      dimnames = list(NULL, panel_c_gene_order)
    )
  )
  saveRDS(panel_c_effects_cache, panel_c_effects_rds, compress = "xz")
}

panel_c_effects <- panel_c_effects |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene = factor(
      as.character(.data$gene),
      levels = c("16-gene covered subset", panel_c_gene_order)
    ),
    contrast = factor(
      as.character(.data$contrast),
      levels = panel_c_contrast_levels
    ),
    contrast_lab = factor(
      unname(panel_c_contrast_labs[as.character(.data$contrast)]),
      levels = unname(panel_c_contrast_labs)
    )
  )

stopifnot(nrow(panel_c_effects) == 4L * (1L + length(panel_c_gene_order)))
stopifnot(all(panel_c_gene_order %in% as.character(panel_c_effects$gene)))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(unlist(panel_c_effects[c(
  "estimate", ".lower", ".upper", "tail_p", "q_value"
)]))))

panel_c_effects |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$is_aggregate) |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$contrast, .data$estimate, .data$.lower, .data$.upper,
    .data$tail_p, .data$q_value, .data$n_case, .data$n_reference
  )
```

## C6. Plot the four aligned contrasts

```{r}
#| label: panel-c-helpers

plot_panel_c_logmu <- function(effects_df) {
  gene_levels <- levels(effects_df$gene)
  agg_df <- effects_df |> dplyr::filter(.data$is_aggregate)
  gene_df <- effects_df |> dplyr::filter(!.data$is_aggregate)
  x_rng <- range(c(effects_df$.lower, effects_df$.upper), finite = TRUE)
  x_pad <- diff(x_rng) * 0.05

  ggplot2::ggplot(effects_df, ggplot2::aes(y = .data$gene)) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      colour = col_mid,
      linetype = "22",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(
      data = gene_df,
      ggplot2::aes(xmin = .data$.lower, xmax = .data$.upper, x = .data$estimate),
      colour = col_dark,
      linewidth = 0.35
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = gene_df,
      ggplot2::aes(x = .data$estimate),
      shape = 16,
      size = 1.35,
      colour = col_dark
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(
      data = agg_df,
      ggplot2::aes(xmin = .data$.lower, xmax = .data$.upper, x = .data$estimate),
      colour = col_untreated,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = agg_df,
      ggplot2::aes(x = .data$estimate),
      shape = 23,
      size = 2.2,
      fill = col_untreated,
      colour = col_dark,
      stroke = 0.4
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(cols = ggplot2::vars(.data$contrast_lab)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(gene_levels)) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(x_rng[1] - x_pad, x_rng[2] + x_pad),
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = expression(log[2] ~ "fold change (offset-centred" ~ mu * ")"),
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_multipanel +
    ggplot2::theme(
      strip.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 5.5),
      panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(0.4, "lines"),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 4, 2)
    )
}
```

## C7. Calibration-gated result

```{r}
#| label: panel-c-result-text
#| include: false

panel_c_aggregate_row <- function(contrast_name) {
  panel_c_effects |>
    dplyr::filter(
      .data$is_aggregate,
      as.character(.data$contrast) == contrast_name
    ) |>
    dplyr::slice(1)
}

panel_c_format_result <- function(x) {
  sprintf(
    "%.2f (95%% interval %.2f to %.2f; q = %s)",
    x$estimate,
    x$.lower,
    x$.upper,
    format.pval(x$q_value, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)
  )
}

panel_c_result_calibration <- panel_c_aggregate_row("study control - HCA")
panel_c_result_primary <- panel_c_aggregate_row("untreated - study control")
panel_c_result_hca <- panel_c_aggregate_row("untreated - HCA")
panel_c_result_treatment <- panel_c_aggregate_row("paired untreated - treated")
```

**Reading Panel c.** Interpret study control − HCA first. If that calibration
contrast remains shifted, untreated − HCA contains residual reference-domain
shift and is a sensitivity analysis; untreated − study control remains the
primary disease contrast. The paired treatment contrast is supported only when
its subject-coupled aggregate interval excludes zero. Gene-wise `q_value` is
an exploratory BH adjustment of empirical two-sided sign-tail probabilities
across the 16 genes within each contrast; aggregate values use the four
prespecified signature contrasts. These are modular posterior-tail summaries,
not likelihood-ratio p-values with a frequentist FDR guarantee.

**Current result.** Calibration does not pass on the expression scale: the
study-control − HCA aggregate is
`r panel_c_format_result(panel_c_result_calibration)`, showing that the
comprehensive HCA reference is systematically lower than the SAVI study controls
for this signature. The primary untreated − study-control contrast is
`r panel_c_format_result(panel_c_result_primary)`; the larger untreated − HCA
contrast, `r panel_c_format_result(panel_c_result_hca)`, therefore contains both
disease-associated signal and reference-domain shift. The paired untreated −
treated contrast is `r panel_c_format_result(panel_c_result_treatment)`, consistent
with attenuation after treatment in these four paired subjects, but it is not a
population-wide treatment-efficacy claim.

```{r}
#| label: panel-c-audit

panel_c_agg <- panel_c_effects |> dplyr::filter(.data$is_aggregate)

panel_c_direction <- panel_c_effects |>
  dplyr::filter(!.data$is_aggregate) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    direction = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$q_value <= 0.05 & .data$estimate > 0 ~ "positive",
      .data$q_value <= 0.05 & .data$estimate < 0 ~ "negative",
      TRUE ~ "unresolved"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::count(.data$contrast, .data$direction) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = .data$direction,
    values_from = .data$n,
    values_fill = 0L
  )

list(
  aggregate = panel_c_agg |>
    dplyr::select(
      .data$contrast, .data$estimate, .data$.lower, .data$.upper,
      .data$tail_p, .data$q_value, .data$n_case, .data$n_reference,
      .data$uncertainty_method
    ),
  constituent_directions = panel_c_direction,
  artifacts = tibble::tibble(
    artifact = c("se_monocytic", "sample_log_rate_audit", "hca_draws", "effects"),
    path = c(
      panel_c_se_rds,
      panel_c_sample_logmu_rds,
      panel_c_hca_logmu_rds,
      panel_c_effects_rds
    ),
    exists = file.exists(c(
      panel_c_se_rds,
      panel_c_sample_logmu_rds,
      panel_c_hca_logmu_rds,
      panel_c_effects_rds
    ))
  )
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Panel f — Subject and family influence

**Purpose.** Ask whether Panel c's two main signature estimands
(untreated − comprehensive HCA; untreated − study control) depend on one or a
few of the 12 biological subjects. HCA draws stay fixed; only the SAVI target
side is refit after each deletion.

**Method.** Collapse libraries to one subject×state column (sum counts; sum
exposures). For each deletion, recompute gene-wise untreated and control
locations with `edgeR::mglmOneGroup`, then form log2 contrasts. Deleted
medians are the leave-one-out point estimates. Full-data diamonds and intervals
come from Panel c. Gene rows on the main plot are the 16-gene aggregate plus up
to five constituents selected by deletion range \(R_g\), preferring genes whose
direction category flips.

## F1. Subjects and deletion sets

```{r}
#| label: panel-f-subjects

# Harmonise control IDs (C8/C9) to short display names used in the cohort table.
panel_f_meta <- panel_c_sample_meta |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    person = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("^P1", .data$sample_id) ~ "P1",
      grepl("^P2", .data$sample_id) ~ "P2",
      grepl("^P4", .data$sample_id) ~ "P4",
      grepl("^P5", .data$sample_id) ~ "P5",
      grepl("^P6", .data$sample_id) ~ "P6",
      grepl("^C8", .data$sample_id) ~ "C8",
      grepl("^C9", .data$sample_id) ~ "C9",
      TRUE ~ .data$sample_id
    )
  )

panel_f_people <- sort(unique(panel_f_meta$person))

# Named deletion sets: 12 single-person deletions + two family sets (audit).
panel_f_deletions <- c(
  stats::setNames(lapply(panel_f_people, identity), panel_f_people),
  list(
    `C8+C9` = c("C8", "C9"),
    `P1/P2/C8/C9` = c("P1", "P2", "C8", "C9")
  )
)

tibble::tibble(
  n_people = length(panel_f_people),
  people = paste(panel_f_people, collapse = ", "),
  n_deletion_sets = length(panel_f_deletions)
)
```

## F2. Subject×state counts for the 16 genes

```{r}
#| label: panel-f-subject-counts

panel_f_feature_ids <- panel_c_feature_map$.feature[
  match(panel_c_gene_order, panel_c_feature_map$gene)
]

# One column per person × group; repeated libraries are added on the count and
# exposure scales (same rule as Panel c).
panel_f_keys <- panel_f_meta |>
  dplyr::distinct(.data$person, .data$group) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$group, .data$person)

panel_f_counts <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(panel_f_keys)), function(i) {
  idx <- which(
    panel_f_meta$person == panel_f_keys$person[[i]] &
      panel_f_meta$group == panel_f_keys$group[[i]]
  )
  rowSums(panel_c_counts[panel_f_feature_ids, panel_f_meta$col_id[idx], drop = FALSE])
})
colnames(panel_f_counts) <- paste(
  panel_f_keys$person, panel_f_keys$group, sep = "__"
)
rownames(panel_f_counts) <- panel_c_gene_order

panel_f_keys$offset <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(panel_f_keys)), function(i) {
  idx <- which(
    panel_f_meta$person == panel_f_keys$person[[i]] &
      panel_f_meta$group == panel_f_keys$group[[i]]
  )
  off <- panel_f_meta$offset[idx]
  max(off) + log(sum(exp(off - max(off))))
})

panel_f_hca_median <- panel_c_hca_draws |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$gene) |>
  dplyr::summarise(hca_log_mu = stats::median(.data$hca_log_mu), .groups = "drop")

tibble::tibble(
  n_genes = nrow(panel_f_counts),
  n_subject_state = ncol(panel_f_counts),
  n_untreated = sum(panel_f_keys$group == "untreated"),
  n_control = sum(panel_f_keys$group == "control")
)
```

## F3. Leave-one-out log2 effects (HCA fixed)

```{r}
#| label: panel-f-leave-one-out

panel_f_group_logmu <- function(keep_people, group_name) {
  hit <- panel_f_keys$person %in% keep_people & panel_f_keys$group == group_name
  y <- panel_f_counts[, hit, drop = FALSE]
  off <- panel_f_keys$offset[hit]
  vapply(panel_c_gene_order, function(g) {
    as.numeric(edgeR::mglmOneGroup(
      matrix(y[g, ], nrow = 1L),
      offset = off,
      dispersion = 0.05
    ))
  }, numeric(1))
}

panel_f_effects_one <- function(deleted, label) {
  keep <- setdiff(panel_f_people, deleted)
  log_u <- panel_f_group_logmu(keep, "untreated")
  log_c <- panel_f_group_logmu(keep, "control")
  hca <- panel_f_hca_median$hca_log_mu[
    match(panel_c_gene_order, panel_f_hca_median$gene)
  ]

  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(
      gene = panel_c_gene_order,
      contrast = "untreated - HCA",
      estimate = (log_u - hca) / log(2),
      deletion = label
    ),
    tibble::tibble(
      gene = panel_c_gene_order,
      contrast = "untreated - study control",
      estimate = (log_u - log_c) / log(2),
      deletion = label
    )
  )
}

# Full-data point estimates use the same mglm rule (for deletion comparisons).
panel_f_full_points <- panel_f_effects_one(character(0), "full")

# Single-person deletions for the main panel.
panel_f_loo <- lapply(panel_f_people, function(p) {
  panel_f_effects_one(p, p)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Family deletions for the audit table only.
panel_f_family <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  panel_f_effects_one(c("C8", "C9"), "C8+C9"),
  panel_f_effects_one(c("P1", "P2", "C8", "C9"), "P1/P2/C8/C9")
)

panel_f_loo |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$contrast) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_rows = dplyr::n(),
    n_deletions = dplyr::n_distinct(.data$deletion),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## F4. Influence scores and gene selection

```{r}
#| label: panel-f-select-genes

panel_f_direction <- function(estimate, .lower = NA_real_, .upper = NA_real_) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.finite(.lower) & is.finite(.upper) & .lower > 0 ~ "positive",
    is.finite(.lower) & is.finite(.upper) & .upper < 0 ~ "negative",
    is.finite(estimate) & estimate > 0 ~ "positive",
    is.finite(estimate) & estimate < 0 ~ "negative",
    TRUE ~ "unresolved"
  )
}

# Full-data intervals from Panel c (same two estimands).
panel_f_full <- panel_c_effects |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !.data$is_aggregate,
    .data$contrast %in% c("untreated - HCA", "untreated - study control")
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    gene = as.character(.data$gene),
    contrast = as.character(.data$contrast),
    full_estimate = .data$estimate,
    .lower = .data$.lower,
    .upper = .data$.upper,
    full_direction = panel_f_direction(.data$estimate, .data$.lower, .data$.upper)
  )

panel_f_agg_full <- panel_c_effects |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$is_aggregate,
    .data$contrast %in% c("untreated - HCA", "untreated - study control")
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    gene = "16-gene covered subset",
    contrast = as.character(.data$contrast),
    full_estimate = .data$estimate,
    .lower = .data$.lower,
    .upper = .data$.upper,
    full_direction = panel_f_direction(.data$estimate, .data$.lower, .data$.upper)
  )

panel_f_loo_summary <- panel_f_loo |>
  dplyr::left_join(panel_f_full, by = c("gene", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    deleted_direction = panel_f_direction(.data$estimate),
    direction_changed = .data$deleted_direction != .data$full_direction
  )

panel_f_gene_scores <- panel_f_loo_summary |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$gene, .data$contrast) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    R = max(.data$estimate) - min(.data$estimate),
    any_flip = any(.data$direction_changed),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = .data$contrast,
    values_from = c(.data$R, .data$any_flip)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    R_g = pmax(
      .data$`R_untreated - HCA`,
      .data$`R_untreated - study control`,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    any_flip = .data$`any_flip_untreated - HCA` |
      .data$`any_flip_untreated - study control`
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$any_flip), dplyr::desc(.data$R_g), .data$gene)

panel_f_selected_genes <- panel_f_gene_scores |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 5L) |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$gene)

# Influential deletion label: person whose deleted estimate is farthest from full.
panel_f_influencer <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  panel_f_loo_summary,
  panel_f_loo |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$contrast, .data$deletion) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      gene = "16-gene covered subset",
      estimate = mean(.data$estimate),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(panel_f_agg_full, by = c("gene", "contrast"))
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$gene, .data$contrast) |>
  dplyr::mutate(abs_shift = abs(.data$estimate - .data$full_estimate)) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(.data$abs_shift, n = 1L, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    .data$gene, .data$contrast,
    influential_deletion = .data$deletion
  )

panel_f_gene_scores |>
  dplyr::select(.data$gene, .data$R_g, .data$any_flip) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 8L)
```

## F5. Plot table (aggregate + selected genes)

```{r}
#| label: panel-f-plot-data

panel_f_plot_genes <- c("16-gene covered subset", panel_f_selected_genes)

# Aggregate leave-one-out: equal-weight mean of the 16 gene effects.
panel_f_loo_agg <- panel_f_loo |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$contrast, .data$deletion) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    gene = "16-gene covered subset",
    estimate = mean(.data$estimate),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(panel_f_agg_full, by = c("gene", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    deleted_direction = panel_f_direction(.data$estimate),
    direction_changed = .data$deleted_direction != .data$full_direction
  )

panel_f_loo_sel <- panel_f_loo_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene %in% panel_f_selected_genes)

panel_f_range <- dplyr::bind_rows(panel_f_loo_agg, panel_f_loo_sel) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$gene, .data$contrast) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    loo_min = min(.data$estimate),
    loo_max = max(.data$estimate),
    n_flip = sum(.data$direction_changed),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

panel_f_full_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(panel_f_agg_full, panel_f_full) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene %in% panel_f_plot_genes) |>
  dplyr::left_join(panel_f_range, by = c("gene", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(panel_f_influencer, by = c("gene", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene = factor(.data$gene, levels = rev(panel_f_plot_genes)),
    contrast_lab = factor(
      dplyr::case_when(
        .data$contrast == "untreated - HCA" ~ "Untreated - HCA",
        .data$contrast == "untreated - study control" ~ "Untreated - CTRL"
      ),
      levels = c("Untreated - HCA", "Untreated - CTRL")
    ),
    row_flip = .data$n_flip > 0
  )

panel_f_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(panel_f_loo_agg, panel_f_loo_sel) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene %in% panel_f_plot_genes) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene = factor(.data$gene, levels = rev(panel_f_plot_genes)),
    contrast_lab = factor(
      dplyr::case_when(
        .data$contrast == "untreated - HCA" ~ "Untreated - HCA",
        .data$contrast == "untreated - study control" ~ "Untreated - CTRL"
      ),
      levels = c("Untreated - HCA", "Untreated - CTRL")
    )
  )

saveRDS(
  list(
    gene_scores = panel_f_gene_scores,
    selected_genes = panel_f_selected_genes,
    full_plot = panel_f_full_plot,
    loo_points = panel_f_points,
    family = panel_f_family
  ),
  panel_f_effects_rds,
  compress = "xz"
)

panel_f_full_plot |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$gene, .data$contrast_lab, .data$full_estimate,
    .data$loo_min, .data$loo_max, .data$n_flip, .data$influential_deletion
  )
```

## F6. Plot

```{r}
#| label: panel-f-helpers

plot_panel_f_influence <- function(full_df, points_df) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(full_df, ggplot2::aes(y = .data$gene)) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      colour = col_mid,
      linetype = "22",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(
      ggplot2::aes(xmin = .data$loo_min, xmax = .data$loo_max),
      colour = col_light,
      linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(
      ggplot2::aes(xmin = .data$.lower, xmax = .data$.upper),
      colour = col_dark,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = points_df,
      ggplot2::aes(x = .data$estimate),
      shape = 1,
      size = 1.4,
      colour = col_mid,
      stroke = 0.35
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$full_estimate,
        fill = .data$row_flip
      ),
      shape = 23,
      size = 2.2,
      colour = col_dark,
      stroke = 0.4
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$loo_max,
        label = .data$influential_deletion
      ),
      hjust = -0.15,
      size = 1.8,
      colour = col_mid
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = col_dark, `TRUE` = col_treated),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(cols = ggplot2::vars(.data$contrast_lab)) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = expression(log[2] ~ "fold change"),
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_multipanel +
    ggplot2::theme(
      strip.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 5.5),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 18, 4, 2)
    )
}
```

# Reviewer-facing self-review

| Dimension | Review question | Status and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Contribution | Does Panel b add information beyond the original study control? | **Pass with boundary.** It evaluates two external HCA targets, but calibration correctly prevents an unqualified disease claim. |
| Writing clarity | Can the analyses be reproduced from the report? | **Pass.** Panel b records the 23- and 26-label maps, 15-part likelihood, target weights, draw pairing, ROPE and FDR family. Panel c records its cohort estimand, repeat-library rule, subject resampling, HCA standardisation and multiplicity families. |
| Experimental strength | Is the external baseline validated against an internal healthy benchmark? | **Pass.** Study-control calibration is reported before disease contrasts; 4/7 comprehensive and 5/7 personalised calibration discoveries are retained as a failure mode. |
| Evaluation completeness | Are important design choices stress-tested? | **Needs evidence.** The 15-part harmonisation is biologically explicit, but the previous coarse residual model should remain a supplementary resolution-sensitivity analysis. Panel c still has only four paired subjects and no joint HCA gene model. |
| Method soundness | Are compositional mass, biological units and cross-model uncertainty handled correctly? | **Pass within scope.** Panel b closes counts over 15 parts and uses 12 independent subjects. Panel c collapses repeat libraries, couples all genes to the same subject resample, and independently samples separate HCA gene posteriors without pretending they form a joint posterior. |

## Panel-b claim–evidence map

| Claim | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SAVI and HCA are compared on a shared biological estimand. | Explicit coverage checks map all 23 SAVI labels and all 26 HCA L3 labels to the same 15-part composition. | Supported |
| The comprehensive baseline equal-averages observed age/sex profiles rather than donor-weighting the HCA population. | Each observed age-decade × sex profile receives weight `1 / n_profiles` before response-scale averaging within draws. | Supported |
| Demographic personalisation does not remove reference-domain shift in this case. | Calibration yields 4/7 discoveries for comprehensive HCA and 5/7 for personalised HCA. | Supported |
| HCA contrasts alone establish SAVI disease effects. | Calibration fails; HCA contrasts are therefore labelled sensitivity analyses and the study-control contrast remains primary. | Not supported; claim explicitly rejected |

## Panel-c claim–evidence map

| Claim | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The SAVI uncertainty unit is the biological subject. | Repeat libraries are collapsed within subject×state, and every Bayesian-bootstrap replicate uses the same subject weights for all 16 genes. | Supported |
| The signature interval represents uncertainty across subjects, not variability across a fixed gene list. | The 16-gene mean is recalculated inside each subject-coupled Bayesian-bootstrap replicate; genes are not treated as exchangeable bootstrap units. | Supported |
| Panel c uses the same comprehensive demographic target as Panel b. | HCA log-μ draws use Panel b's observed healthy-HCA age×sex profiles and exact target weights, with ethnicity equal-standardised and dataset random effects excluded. | Supported |
| The untreated − HCA interval is a fully Bayesian joint-model interval. | The SAVI side is a Bayesian bootstrap and the 16 HCA genes come from separate fits; the code independently pairs these sources and labels the interval modular hybrid. | Not supported; claim explicitly rejected |
| A treatment-associated attenuation is present in the paired observations. | The four-patient paired aggregate interval excludes zero, while the report explicitly limits the claim to these four subjects. | Supported with a severe sample-size boundary |
